A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dita and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The complete material supports comparison, including matching relocated experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation evaluations, real-robot experiments, and appendix ablations, including Dita results in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds wrist-camera evaluation, CALVIN experiments in Table 7, and failure cases in Figure 12.

M1.justification: The proposed tokenization, in-context diffusion Transformer, objective, and denoising procedure remain unchanged. The wrist-camera and depth experiments evaluate configurations of the existing flexible architecture; no new method component is specified.

E1.justification: The datasets and robot tasks are retained. Table 2 adds LIBERO evaluation with wrist-camera observations alongside the original third-person-only configuration, modestly extending sensory test coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 7 evaluates a comparator labeled AdaLN DiT [17] against Dita on CALVIN, reporting average lengths of 1.45 and 2.56 respectively. Existing comparator sets, including the diffusion-head comparisons in Table 9, remain.

E3.justification: Added settings include wrist-camera LIBERO evaluation and CALVIN augmentation controls and 2-, 6-, 12-, and 24-layer configurations, including runs without pretraining. The existing CALVIN ABC→D, 1,000-chain protocol is retained. ManiSkill2 setup details are relocated to Appendix B.4, not revised.

E4.justification: Table 7 adds direct depth-scaling, augmentation, and conditioning comparisons, substantially extending checks of the paper's scaling premise. Appendix D.3 and Figure 12 add dedicated grasping and pouring failure cases. Earlier analyses remain, including the denoising study moved to Table 12.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation practices are added or revised. The new numerical results continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing matched results remain unchanged. Additions include 92.3% average LIBERO success with wrist inputs, CALVIN depth averages of 1.84, 2.21, 2.56, and 2.61, the AdaLN comparison, and failure examples. These are additional conditions, not same-setting improvements. Table 7's new augmentation row is internally inconsistent.

T1.justification: The noise-prediction objective and Equation 1 are unchanged, with no added formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs. Replacing 'timestamp' with 'timestep' changes terminology rather than mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of scalable in-context diffusion, benchmark generalization, and few-shot real-robot adaptation. The additional experiments support existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.3 identifies inaccurate grasp positioning despite recovery attempts and unstable pouring during motion as failure mechanisms. Existing interpretations concerning model capacity, LoRA, generalization, and denoising are retained.

D1.justification: Table 7 newly identifies the retained 3.61 CALVIN result as without augmentation and specifies depth and pretraining conditions for added configurations. Existing optimization, hardware, and access information remains; the detailed ManiSkill2 setup is merely relocated.

R1.justification: The same 85 references and related-work positioning are retained. The added AdaLN comparison reuses citation [17]; it does not introduce new cited literature or revise the novelty discussion.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording, terminology, and affiliation edits, adds an acknowledgment and failure-analysis subsection, and moves ManiSkill2 setup and denoising discussion into the appendix. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, Figure 12, and a wrist-camera row in Table 2. The denoising table moves from main-text Table 6 to appendix Table 12, other displays shift, and Figure 3's timestep label is corrected. The existing visual design is preserved.

improvement.justification: The added depth and conditioning comparisons provide useful checks of existing claims, while explicit failure cases improve transparency. The gain is limited by sparse explanation of new configurations and Table 7's inconsistent augmentation row: 69.0% five-task success exceeds 67.3% four-task success, and the rates do not yield the reported 3.78 average.
